predecessors.note: Cliopatria's French Fifth Republic 1961-2023 shape still contains all of Djibouti (see notes).

capitals.name: Djibouti City
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Djibouti City'; the country is 'named for its capital, the City of Djibouti'.

correction.text: new keyframe, years only: the shape of Cliopatria's 1979 row holds from independence on 27 June 1977

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox 'Independence from France: 27 June 1977'; 'A third independence referendum was held ... on 8 May 1977' with 98.8% for disengagement from France. Cliopatria's row starts in 1979.

22,222 km2 against the infobox 23,200 km2 (ratio 0.96). The gazetteer shows 92 cells against 86 for the country: 6 cells (about 1,500 km2) on the southern edge lie over Ethiopia, a border-precision difference, not an error of extent.

22,134 km2 (ratio 0.95 to the infobox). It differs from the 1979 shape by 0.4% (bbox west edge 41.86 to 41.83 E); the civil-war page records no territorial change from the war, and no page opened dates a border change in 1992.

region.text: the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas, renamed in 1967

ledger.note: 1977: Djibouti becomes independent from France. Infobox 'Independence from France: 27 June 1977'; the referendum of 8 May 1977 gave '98.8% of the electorate' for disengagement; Hassan Gouled Aptidon 'became the nation's first president (1977-1999)'.

region.text: the north of the country: Obock and the siege of Tadjoura

ledger.note: 1991: FRUD rebels attack in the north. 'the FRUD launched, on the 21 November 1991, an assault of the town of Obock'; the army had captured 232 individuals on 15-16 November. The page names the towns, not the districts: Obock and Tadjourah are the researcher's reading.

region.text: the north: the military posts the rebels seized and the sieges of Tadjoura and Obock

ledger.note: 1992: the north falls to FRUD. 'The FRUD seized all military posts in the north of the country and laid siege to the city of Tadjoura and Obock' (no exact date; clashes near Tadjoura on 3-4 January 1992; French troops deployed in the north in February 1992).

region.text: the rebel-held areas of the north

ledger.note: 1993: the army drives FRUD back. 'On the 5 July 1993, the government launched a massive counter-offensive in the areas controlled by the rebels'; the main FRUD base at Assa-Gueyla was captured and the rebels 'take refuge in the mountains on the border with Eritrea in the north'. The refuge is not mapped.

1994: the first peace. 'an initial Abb'a peace agreement was signed on December 26, 1994'; Ahmed Dini's faction refused it and fought on until 'a definitive peace agreement was signed' on 12 May 2001. The Mount Mabla offensive of 3-10 March 1994 had failed.

wars.name: Djiboutian Civil War
wars.outcome: No territorial change: the July 1993 counter-offensive drove FRUD back into the mountains on the Eritrean border, the Abb'a agreement ended the main war on 26 December 1994 and a final agreement with Dini's faction followed on 12 May 2001.
wars.note: Infobox start 31 October 1991; the Djibouti page says 'The war lasted from 1991 to 2001'. France deployed troops in the north in February 1992 and mediated the 1994 agreement; Ethiopian and Djiboutian troops operated against FRUD groups on both sides of the border in 1997-98.

certainty.note: The frontiers are colonial lines; the civil-war page mentions an agreement 'on the definition of its common border' with Ethiopia around 1997 (no exact date). The pages opened do not discuss the Eritrean frontier (the 2008 Ras Doumeira clash was not opened): a gap-filler should.

notes: Cliopatria's Republic of Djibouti starts in 1979 but independence is 27 June 1977: the 1977-78 keyframe is new, and the land in 1977-78 must come from the French Fifth Republic. Cliopatria's French Fifth Republic 1961-2023 shape still contains all of Djibouti (gazetteer: the 86 cells of the country lie inside it in 1970 and in 1980, so it overlaps this row from 1979 to 2023): eu-22 (French Fifth Republic) must remove Djibouti from its shape. The rebel front FRUD held the north for about a year and a half (late 1991 to July 1993) and has its own rebel dossier. Not opened for budget: the 2008 Djibouti-Eritrea clash at Ras Doumeira, and the 'French Territory of the Afars and the Issas' page (1967-77), which is the other state's life (French Africa / French Fifth Republic dossiers). The Djibouti page gives the civil war as 1991-2001; the civil-war page opens with October 1991. The seed lists Eritrea, Ethiopia, Somalia and Yemen as neighbours; no border event with any of them is on the pages opened.
